hints.title: Level Inversion Symmetry
hints.text: At depth d, values span from 2^(d-1) to 2^d - 1. A node label has a symmetric inverted counterpart within that level.

hints.title: Complement Identity
hints.text: The mirrored counterpart of value x at depth d is calculated as min_val + max_val - x.

hints.title: Parent Calculation
hints.text: In standard binary trees parent is x // 2. Under zigzag reversal, the parent is the inverted counterpart divided by 2.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def pathInZigZagTree(self, label: int) -> list[int]:
        res = []
        curr = label
        while curr >= 1:
            res.append(curr)
            depth = curr.bit_length()
            min_val = 1 << (depth - 1)
            max_val = (1 << depth) - 1
            curr = (min_val + max_val - curr) // 2
        return res[::-1]
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Constructing or traversing the infinite binary tree top-down explores extraneous nodes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Mathematical level inversion computes the parent label directly in O(1) time per tree height level.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize binary tree bit depth relationships and the level inversion formula.
complexity.notes: Path is reconstructed bottom-up from label to 1 and reversed.
